key_insight: CoopEval introduces the first comprehensive benchmark showing that contemporary LLMs—despite stronger reasoning—tend to defect in single-shot social dilemmas, and evaluates mechanisms that can sustain cooperation among LLM agents.
problem_solved: Addresses the safety and coordination gap where powerful LLM agents behave uncooperatively in mixed-motive settings (e.g., prisoner's dilemma, public goods), by providing a standardized evaluation suite to measure and compare cooperation-sustaining interventions.
method: Design CoopEval: a benchmark suite of canonical social dilemmas (single-shot and repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, public goods, commons) and standardized metrics for cooperation and payoff.

Implement and evaluate a range of cooperation-sustaining mechanisms (e.g., communication/commitment channels, incentive modifications, reputation/history conditioning) across multiple LLM agents, with/without explicit reasoning prompts.
Compare agent behaviours and mechanism effectiveness using quantitative cooperation rates, payoffs, and robustness analyses to identify which interventions successfully promote sustained cooperation.
impact: Provides practitioners a replicable toolkit to assess and improve multi-agent safety and coordination in LLM-driven systems, guiding design choices (mechanisms, prompts, incentives) to reduce defection and align group outcomes.
visual_elements: Payoff matrix icon + simple Prisoner's Dilemma diagram showing defect vs cooperate outcomes
Bar chart comparing cooperation rates across LLM models and baseline (with/without reasoning)
Flowchart of evaluated mechanisms (communication, commitment, incentives, reputation) mapping to their observed effect sizes
Timeline/sequence diagram contrasting single-shot vs repeated interactions and resulting cooperation dynamics
paper_title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
paper_authors: Emanuel Tewolde, Xiao Zhang, David Guzman Piedrahita, Vincent Conitzer, Zhijing Jin
